blocks.x: Logarithm The logarithm of a number b to base a, written log_a b, is the index/power c to which base a must be raised to give b: log_a b = c ⇒ b = a^c, provided a ≠ 1 and a > 0.
Exponential equation An equation in which a variable appears as an exponent. Solved either by equating exponents on a common base, or by taking logarithms of both sides.
Quadratic equation An equation of the form ax² + bx + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a ≠ 0.
Indices→ Logarithms→ Exponential Equations→ Quadratic Equations
Indices and logarithms are the toolkit; exponential and quadratic equations are where they get applied.
A logarithm asks: "what power gets me there?" Master the definition, the four laws, and the two special properties.

log_a b = c
⇒ b = a<sup>c</sup>, provided a ≠ 1 and b > 0.
Remark: the base can be any positive number except 1. The logarithm of a negative number does not exist. When no base is written, it means base 10.

Law 1 — Product
log_a x + log_a y = log_a(xy)

items: 1Same base, so multiply the arguments.log₂3 + log₂4 = log₂(3×4)

blocks.x:
Law 2 — Quotient
log_a x − log_a y = log_a(x/y)

items: 1Same base, so divide the arguments.log₄21 − log₄7 = log₄(21÷7)

blocks.x:
Law 3 — Power
log_a x<sup>n</sup> = n·log_a x

items: 1Bring the exponent down as a multiplier.log₂5² = 2·log₂5

blocks.x:
Law 4 — Change of base
log_a x = log_b x / log_b a

items: 1Apply the change-of-base law with a=2, x=8, new base b=3.log₂8 = log₃8 / log₃2

blocks.x: log_b b = 1 — the logarithm of any number to the base of that same number is 1.
log_b 1 = 0 — the logarithm of 1 to any base other than 1 is zero.
Try it yourself — use the laws above
Eight properties of indices — the toolkit you need before solving exponential equations by the same-base method.

items: 1A negative power gives the reciprocal of the positive power.2⁻³ = 1/2³
1Distribute the power over numerator and denominator.(2/7)² = 2²/7²
1Flip the fraction and drop the minus sign.(3/2)⁻³ = 2³/3³
1To raise a power to a power, multiply the exponents.(3³)² = 3³×² = 3⁶

blocks.x: An exponential equation is one in which a variable appears as an exponent. Two methods solve it: matching bases, or taking logarithms.
If b<sup>x</sup> = b<sup>y</sup>, then x = y (where b > 0 and b ≠ 1). If the bases are the same, set the exponents equal.

items: 1Both sides already share base 2, so equate the exponents.2x = 4

blocks.x: Rewrite both sides with a common base

blocks.x: Try it yourself — isolate, then take logs
Three roads to the same roots
A quadratic equation has the form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a, b, c real, a ≠ 0). We solve it three ways: factorization, completing the square, and the quadratic formula.
Express ax² + bx + c = 0 as a product of its linear factors (x−k)(x−h), where h and k are the roots.

items: 1Split the middle term into two terms whose coefficients multiply to 12 and add to 8.x² + 6x + 2x + 12 = 0
If the coefficient of x² is not 1, divide both sides by that coefficient.
Isolate all variable terms on one side, constants on the other.
Complete the square: add (half the coefficient of x)² to both sides.
2Half of 6 is 3; add 3² = 9 to both sides.x² + 6x + 9 = −8 + 9
3Factor the left side as a perfect square.(x+3)² = 1
4Take the square root of both sides.x + 3 = ±√1

blocks.x: Try it yourself — complete the square

For ax² + bx + c = 0, obtained by completing the square in general:

x = −b ± √(b² − 4ac)2a
Example: find the roots of x² + 6x + 8 = 0
x₁ = −2, x₂ = −4 — matches the completing-the-square result
Try it yourself — use the quadratic formula

Discriminant check: in the quadratic formula, the expression under the root, b²−4ac, is the discriminant. If it is positive, there are two distinct real roots; if zero, one repeated real root; if negative, no real roots.
